learning: Ask whether oscillation on the slalom falls below iteration 0's 0.163, whether the lighter body needed a different kp, and whether progress on the s-bend recovers toward 0.185 while line loss stays at or below 1.
notes: Restores the 4 cm row and keeps the +/-0.03 m spread, with the lighter, shorter body the Builder proposed. kp 2.5 and kd 0.15 are set for the wider spread and 4 cm lookahead, based on iterations 0 and 1.
rationale: Iteration 0 (y=0.04, +/-0.02 m, 4 cm row) gave s-bend progress 0.185, the best progress seen, but 2 line-loss events per s-bend and slalom run. Iteration 1 (y=0.02, +/-0.03 m) cut s-bend line loss to 1 but collapsed s-bend progress to 0.04, so the shorter row or the lower kp/base_speed mix hurt bends. I adopt the Builder's intent: restore the 4 cm row and keep the +/-0.03 m spread at 15 mm spacing. The Builder's body change (length 0.14 m, mass 0.6 kg) cuts yaw inertia from about 0.031 to about 0.017 kg m^2, so the same wheel differential turns faster. To keep the signal scale the Builder needs, I use kp 2.5, since the wider spread gives a lower signal per metre of offset (about 67 weight per metre against 100 in iteration 0). I set kd to 0.15 because the 4 cm lookahead needed that damping in iteration 0. The lighter robot is more responsive, so I lower base_speed only slightly, from 1.6 to 1.5, to limit overshoot while keeping enough speed for the 3 s limit. Weights stay symmetric at [-2,-1,0,1,2] and line_loss stays last_direction, which recovered from short losses in iteration 0. Expected result is progress and line loss better than iteration 1 and a score near iteration 0, but I state no measured outcome for this candidate.
